evidence: app/package.json:5 — nuxt ^4.6.3, the current stable line (4.6.3 released 2026-10-27, per github.com/nuxt/nuxt/releases)
app/nuxt.config.ts:1-19 — Nuxt 4 layout: `app/` srcDir, `runtimeConfig`, `compatibilityDate`, `useHead` via `app.head`
app/app/pages/index.vue:10-13 — `await useAsyncData(key, handler)` with `watch`, the current data-loading primitive
app/app/components/PokemonCard.vue:5-11 — `<script setup lang="ts">` with type-only `defineProps`, current component syntax

app/app/lib/pokeapi.ts:72 — raw `fetch` inside the handler; the Nuxt 4 docs pattern is `(_nuxtApp, { signal }) => $fetch(…, { signal })` — the abort signal is never threaded through (nuxt.com/docs/4.x/api/composables/use-async-data/)

app/app/pages/pokemon/[name].vue:116-118 — template-string key plus `watch: [() => route.params.name]`; the docs' newer reactive-key pattern (`useAsyncData(computed(() => …), …)`) covers both concerns
latest_apis.rationale: Genuinely current-generation Nuxt 4.6 with the new `app/` structure and no legacy APIs anywhere; it misses two documented refinements (abortable handlers via `signal`, reactive keys) that postdate most training data.

evidence: app/app/lib/pokeapi.ts:72 — native `fetch` for all HTTP, no axios/polyfills
app/app/lib/pokeapi.ts:48-65 — module-level `Map`/`Set` promise cache with a hand-rolled concurrency limiter using modern async/await
app/app/assets/css/main.css:37-43 — CSS custom properties throughout, plus logical properties (`padding-inline`, `margin-inline`)
app/app/assets/css/main.css:54-61 — `:focus-visible` for accessible focus styling
app/app/pages/index.vue:82-89 — native form controls (`type="search"`, `<select>`) with labels instead of any UI library
app/app/lib/pokeapi.ts:70-71 — request URLs built by string concatenation (`${base}/api/v2${path}`) rather than `URL`/`URLSearchParams`, and no `AbortController`/`AbortSignal` is used anywhere
platform.rationale: The platform is the default everywhere (fetch, Map/Set, custom properties, logical CSS, native form elements); the only misses are never wiring an AbortSignal into fetching and string-built URLs, both cosmetic here.

evidence: app/package.json:5-8 — exactly three dependencies: nuxt, vue, vue-router; zero runtime helpers (no axios, lodash, vueuse, css framework)
app/package.json:7-8 — vue and vue-router declared explicitly although nuxt ships both; the official starter template lists only `nuxt`
dependencies.rationale: Minimal and fully current; the only nit is redundantly pinning vue/vue-router, which duplicates version management nuxt already owns.

evidence: app/app/lib/pokeapi.ts:1-224 — all HTTP access and data shaping behind one module (`api`, `getIndex`, `speciesCardsForRefs`), so an API or fetching-strategy change is contained
app/app/composables/useApiBase.ts:1-8 — the API origin resolved in one composable fed from `nuxt.config.ts:11-15` runtime config

app/app/lib/pokeapi.ts:67 — boundary returns `Promise<any>`; loaders cast freely (`app/app/pages/pokemon/[name].vue:44,48,101-104` `(a: any)`), so API-shape changes surface as runtime bugs, not type errors

app/app/pages/[...slug].vue:1-9 — the 404 pattern (import setResponseStatus + useRequestEvent + status 404) is copy-pasted in five files: also pokemon/[name].vue:120-124, moves/[name].vue:29-35, types/[name].vue:43-47, abilities/[name].vue:34-38

app/app/pages/pokemon/[name].vue:2 — `import { setResponseStatus } from 'h3'` reaches into a transitive dependency that isn't declared in package.json; Nuxt auto-imports this utility (nuxt.com/docs/4.x/api/utils/set-response-status)
app/nuxt.config.ts:2 — `compatibilityDate: '2025-07-15'` is ~15 months stale versus the Nuxt 4.6.x line, deferring newer Nitro behaviours to a future manual bump
churn_resistance.rationale: The data access layer and config centralization are exactly right, but the untyped `any` boundary, five-fold copy-pasted 404/status boilerplate, and reliance on an undeclared transitive package are precisely the things this criterion asks to avoid.

findings.issue: `api()` uses raw `fetch` and never receives the `AbortSignal` that Nuxt 4's `useAsyncData` hands to every handler, so in-flight requests are never cancelled on navigation or refresh.
findings.suggestion: Thread the signal: `useAsyncData(key, (_nuxtApp, { signal }) => load(name, game, signal))` and pass it to `fetch(url, { signal })` (see nuxt.com/docs/4.x/api/composables/use-async-data/#make-your-handler-abortable).

findings.issue: The single data-access module is untyped at the boundary — `Promise<any>` — and every page loader casts with `(a: any)` (e.g. app/app/pages/pokemon/[name].vue:44,101), so API-shape changes fail silently at runtime instead of at compile time.
findings.suggestion: Define interfaces for the PokeAPI resources used (species, pokemon, move, ability, type, generation) and have `api<T>()` return them; drop the `any` casts in the loaders.

findings.issue: The 404-status pattern (import setResponseStatus, `useRequestEvent()`, `if (event) setResponseStatus(event, 404)`, NotFound title) is duplicated in five page files (also pokemon/[name].vue:120, moves/[name].vue:29, types/[name].vue:43, abilities/[name].vue:34).
findings.suggestion: Extract one composable (e.g. `useNotFound(data)`), or throw `createError({ statusCode: 404 })` inside the `useAsyncData` handler and render the app-wide error page, so the pattern lives in one place.

findings.issue: `import { setResponseStatus } from 'h3'` imports a transitive dependency not declared in package.json, coupling app code to h3's module path (h3 v2 is in progress).
findings.suggestion: Rely on Nuxt's auto-import of `setResponseStatus` (documented usage has no import) or import from `#imports`.

findings.issue: `compatibilityDate: '2025-07-15'` is the Nuxt 4.0 release date and ~15 months behind the current 4.6.x stable, so newer Nitro behaviours stay opt-out until a manual bump.
findings.suggestion: Update to the current date when upgrading; Nuxt prompts for this on minor upgrades.

findings.issue: Handlers return `null` for missing resources; Nuxt 4's docs warn that falsy handler results cause the request to be re-run on client hydration (here masked only by the module-level promise cache in pokeapi.ts:48).
findings.suggestion: Return a truthy sentinel (e.g. `{ found: false }`) or throw `createError({ statusCode: 404 })` from the handler so the payload short-circuits client refetches.

findings.issue: Template-string keys plus a `watch` option replicate what the docs' reactive-key pattern (`useAsyncData(computed(() => `pokemon-${route.params.name}`), …)`) does in one step, and the same shape is repeated in three other pages.
findings.suggestion: Use a computed/getter key so refetch-on-param-change is automatic and the `watch` list can go.

findings.issue: `vue` and `vue-router` are declared as direct dependencies even though nuxt ships and pins both, duplicating version management.
findings.suggestion: Keep only `nuxt` in dependencies (as the official starter template does) unless a specific pin is required.

summary: This is current-generation Nuxt (4.6.3, the stable line as of 2026-10-27) written the way the framework wants: `app/` structure, `script setup` + TS, `useAsyncData`/`useHead`/`useState`, one data-access module, one config location, and three dependencies with zero bloat. The forward-looking gaps are polish rather than rot: the fetch layer ignores the abort signals Nuxt now provides, the API boundary is `any`-typed, and the 404/status boilerplate is copy-pasted across five pages. I'd merge it with the signal-threading and typing comments left for a follow-up.

apis.replacement: reactive keys (`computed`/getter key) are the newer documented pattern
